intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Woodruff County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: During our evaluation, nothing came to our attention that would warrant disclosure in this report.
verdicts.detail: A limited review (a “financial and compliance report”), not a full audit: the financial statements in it are unaudited.

limits: From the 2024 report, dated December 2, 2025. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.

cities.name: Cotton Plant
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Mayor. Mayor 1. Per review of payroll records, the city has unpaid federal taxes due totaling $364,360 for taxes, penalties, and interest for prior periods dating between 2015 and 2023. Additionally, tax payments for the current year were not remitted timely, which will likely result in additional penalties and interest.
